A real PostgreSQL proof is MANDATORY: every substantive claim of this node is a runtime privilege behaviour no static check can establish. Both harness paths remain legitimately UNKNOWN because the repository carries TWO admissible real-PG shapes -- suites pairing a *.pg.test.ts with a *-harness.ts and *.probes.json (b3, b4, b5, fibdb052-p1-indexes, portfolio-aggregate, s3refusal) and suites carrying neither (ce1-commercial-account, organization-commercial-acceptance) -- and the CLOSEST SIBLING, which this node extends, is of the second shape. TWO SUBSTRATES, ONE CONTRACT (authority SECTION_10 and SECTION_17). (1) CANONICAL: the L1 behavioural suite runs on its ACTUAL harness image, DEFAULT_IMAGE = postgres:16-alpine, measured at scripts/db-audit-disposable.ts:502 and consumed at tests/postgres/organization-commercial-acceptance.pg.test.ts:714. The R1 manifest froze public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.6.1.143 instead; that was NOT EXECUTABLE, because on that image the role postgres is not a superuser and the fixture's own HOSTED_FIDELITY re-home loop dies with 'must be able to SET ROLE "uellix_owner"' (measured, both images). No impossible setup is frozen as a required gate. (2) OWNER_TOPOLOGY_PROBE: a certification-only substrate with a NON-SUPERUSER function owner, required because the canonical fixture's function owner is postgres and postgres is a SUPERUSER there (rolsuper=t measured), which makes any owner-capability assertion vacuous. (3) SUPPLEMENTAL_FIDELITY: a Supabase-image probe is permitted ONLY when explicitly classified as such and never as the source of a PG-06 pass. IN ALL CASES: DISPOSABLE ONLY, no bind mounts, teardown in finally, leftover check, gated and skipped-never-silently-passed; NEVER hosted staging, NEVER production, NEVER the canonical local Supabase stack; and a substrate that satisfies a control by widening a runtime role is INVALID EVIDENCE. negative_controls.description: STATUS=FUTURE_MATERIALIZATION. SPOOFED ACTOR: an INSERT whose accepted_by_user_id is a subject other than the authenticated one is REFUSED. MUST assert SQLSTATE 23514 AND THE LITERAL MESSAGE 'accepted_by_user_id must be the acting subject (I-T4-6)'. TWO BINDING REASONS, both measured. (1) Before remediation a broken trigger raises 42501 and a correct cross-tenant RLS refusal ALSO raises 42501, so a SQLSTATE-only assertion cannot distinguish a repaired refusal from a shadowed failure. (2) STRENGTHENED IN R3 (blocker B5): THE TOKEN I-T4-6 IS NOT SUFFICIENT EITHER, because the role guard carries the same token. Under M-03 this case moves to 42501 RLS, so a control matching the token, or matching 23514 alone, SURVIVES the mutation. Only the literal message falsifies it. PREMEASURED (authority SECTION_19 R3_M03).

Note the layer: with the trigger repaired this refusal comes from the TRIGGER, not RLS -- RLS-01 is the control that proves the wall underneath.

mutation_controls.description: STATUS=FUTURE_MATERIALIZATION. Remove SECURITY DEFINER from the trigger function (keeping everything else). STATUS=FUTURE_MATERIALIZATION. SUBSTRATE=OWNER_TOPOLOGY_PROBE (a non-superuser owner is required for the states to be distinguishable). Remove SET search_path = public, keeping SECURITY DEFINER. EXPECTED RED: FN-02, plus the semantic arm below. THE SEMANTIC ARM IS A THREE-STATE PROOF AND ALL THREE ARE BINDING -- RE-MEASURED IN R2 (authority SECTION_19 R2_SEARCH_PATH): STATE_1 pin removed, owner CANNOT see the attacker schema => ATTACK REFUSED 23514 digest mismatch; STATE_2 pin removed, owner CAN see it => ATTACK SUCCEEDS and SENTINEL_FORGED_CONTENT_DIGEST is STORED, defeating I-T4-4; STATE_3 pin restored, owner still sees it => ATTACK REFUSED. Only STATE_2 falsifies the pin. A suite running STATE_1 alone observes a harmless failure and concludes the pin is unnecessary -- the exact wrong conclusion. The arm must therefore GRANT the owner USAGE on the shadow schema to reach STATE_2, which is permitted for this probe (authority SECTION_18) and implies nothing for production. UNIQUE ANCHOR: FN-02 plus SENTINEL_FORGED_CONTENT_DIGEST landing in the table in STATE_2 and in no other state.

EXPECTED RED: N-01 and N-05. THE TWO R2 FORMS WERE MEASURED VACUOUS AND ARE PROHIBITED: rewriting IS DISTINCT FROM to <> and dropping the v_actor IS NULL arm both left the spoof and absent probes byte-identical to the unmutated baseline, because accepted_by_user_id is NOT NULL (attnotnull=t) so the two operators cannot differ and the surviving arm covers the NULL case either way. UNIQUE ANCHOR: N-01 and N-05 together, each matched on its LITERAL message -- see their descriptions for why the shared I-T4-6 token is not enough. PREMEASURED (authority SECTION_19 R3_M03).

STATUS=FUTURE_MATERIALIZATION. SUBSTRATE=OWNER_TOPOLOGY_PROBE. NEW IN R3 (blocker B4). Remove C7 -- the owner's RLS-visible read reach -- by dropping the probe-only SELECT policy, once for legal_instrument_versions and once for legal_instruments. EXPECTED RED both times: FN-04 C7 and the probe positive, with 23503 'no published version'. TWO BINDING CONSTRAINTS. (1) THE TWO HALVES ARE OBSERVATIONALLY IDENTICAL -- one JOIN reads both registries, so either invisible side collapses the row to none and yields the same 23503. Each half is anchored by WHICH policy the probe dropped, never by the message; a suite that reports only 'red' cannot tell them apart and must not claim it did. (2) THE REMOVAL MUST NOT BE PERFORMED BY TOGGLING BYPASSRLS, because that would make the control read as evidence that production needs BYPASSRLS, which it does not. What the control MUST discriminate is C7 (23503, visibility) from C3/C4 (42501 naming the table, privilege). UNIQUE ANCHOR: FN-04 C7 plus FN-07.
